title: Decision readiness: one row per requirement, the gate that blocks it, and the number that clears it
rule: Each row's gate and number are read from the file named in `evidence`. `basis = proposed` marks a threshold this build proposes; the owner has not accepted it. A requirement is 'met' only when the register says so; nothing is re-decided here.

rows.requirement: Maintain one collected, organised, analysed list of requirements for the whole project
rows.assessment: This site's requirements page and live/requirements.html both render from data/pipeline/requirements.json; the register is generated, not hand-kept.

rows.requirement: Analyse the requirement list, not just store it (gap, conflict, dependency analysis)
rows.assessment: Every requirement row carries a status and a pointer to the gap that limits it; the decision table turns those gaps into questions with a closing test.

rows.requirement: Ship a dedicated suggestions section that someone reviews before anything is built
rows.assessment: Five suggestions pages exist, none of them auto-applied: the ranked board, the original register, and the per-tree lists.

rows.requirement: Every suggestion must present more than one path so a reviewer can choose, not just approve
rows.assessment: Each board row carries a recommended path AND the alternative it was chosen over, plus reversibility, so a reviewer can pick a different path.

rows.requirement: Publish the questions, the information we have, and the information we do not have, before any decision is made
rows.assessment: Seven decision-critical questions, each with what is known, what is missing and what would close it.

rows.requirement: Suggest concrete ways to discover the missing information, not just note that it is missing
rows.assessment: The 'evidence that would close it' column names a concrete artefact (a ruling, a vendor, a second price source), not just a wish.

rows.requirement: Originate our own NFL lines rather than reuse someone else's numbers
rows.blocking_gate: G3 calibration: the originated side must beat the market benchmark on side error. Model 10.741 vs market 9.792 (n=3165, lab model report).
rows.clearing_number: Side MAE at or below the market benchmark 9.792 on the same window
rows.assessment: A model that originates lines exists and is documented, but it is fitted on a third-party results feed and underperforms the market benchmark on spread error (10.42 vs 9.73), so it is published as a screen rather than a pricing model.

rows.requirement: Research and develop strategies that generate useful signals
rows.blocking_gate: G2 skill above variance: z ≥ 1.96 and an ROI interval excluding zero. Best singles z is -0.57 (S-01-side-1.0).
rows.assessment: Sixteen strategies are registered and evaluated; one passes all eight gates. The signals are hypotheses until gated, and most are rejected.

rows.requirement: Run the strategy set as a leaderboard competition
rows.blocking_gate: Two leaderboards disagree and only one can be cited. Line desk: 0 of 8 strategies through all gates. Landing page (payload): 1 of 16. Flagged as IR-01.
rows.clearing_number: One reconciled leaderboard with at least 1 strategy through G0–G8
rows.assessment: The leaderboard mechanism and gate suite are built and published; the competition cannot rank anything because no strategy has cleared the economic gates, so the result columns are deliberately empty.

rows.requirement: Provide rewards for the top performing strategies
rows.blocking_gate: Q-20 (owner decision): reward rules, funding and legality are not defined in any file.
rows.clearing_number: Written reward rule and legal review recorded (0 of 2 present)
rows.assessment: Reward rules, funding and legality are not defined by anyone. The gate arithmetic is published; paying out is an owner decision (Q-20).

rows.requirement: Cover single bets, parlays and player-prop bet combinations
rows.blocking_gate: Q-21: no prop prices exist from any official source, so no prop combination can be priced. G1 needs 500 props tickets.
rows.assessment: Singles, cross-game parlays and same-game combinations have mathematics and break-even arithmetic. Player props have a model and a calibration but NO market price, so no prop combination can be priced (Q-21).

rows.requirement: Every strategy must pass validation gates before it is allowed to bet
rows.assessment: Eight pre-registered gates; a strategy earns nothing without passing all of them. One of sixteen passes, which is the proof the gates bind.

rows.requirement: Determine correlation values between the signals and markets we use
rows.blocking_gate: Q-21: correlations with market or prop prices cannot be computed without a price feed. Team-stat correlations are published with n.
rows.clearing_number: n published for every market and prop pair (prop/market pairs computed: 0)
rows.assessment: Correlation values are computed for team-stat pairs and published with sample sizes. Player-prop and market correlations cannot be computed without a price feed.

rows.requirement: Remove luck from the equation; keep only selectively skill-based strategies
rows.assessment: Luck removal is implemented: bootstrap intervals, a sign-flip randomisation test, removal of one-score games and blowouts, and a parameter-stability check.

rows.requirement: Track injuries continuously
rows.assessment: The official Week 10 injury report is transcribed in full (345 rows) and re-verified cell by cell in this round; a scheduled workflow refreshes the pipeline data.

rows.requirement: Identify defensive deficiencies caused by backups having to replace starters
rows.assessment: The defensive side of the join is published: club-listed first-string defenders ruled Out are counted, with depth 2-4 losses counted separately.

rows.requirement: Do the same for offense: know whether a starter or a backup is playing
rows.assessment: The offensive side is published the same way; the join is split by unit so a quarterback loss is never averaged with a linebacker loss.

rows.requirement: Produce an executive summary of the important details
rows.assessment: An executive summary and a separate one-page brief exist; the brief is linkable from the landing page.

rows.requirement: Operate with no manual input from the owner
rows.blocking_gate: Snapshot capture: the scheduled refresh completes, but the injury file holds 1 capture date(s) and no fetch time (IR-04).
rows.clearing_number: 5 dated captures, one per day Wednesday to Sunday, with fetch time (proposed; currently 1)
rows.assessment: A scheduled workflow refreshes the data with no manual step, but the schedule is disabled-by-default on a fork and the snapshot date is still fixed in the generator for the pages/ tree.

rows.requirement: Work line by line from official, verified, trusted sources; no hallucinations
rows.assessment: 2,183 cells diffed against an independent transcription of the official pages in this round; a value that cannot be sourced is blank and flagged.

rows.requirement: Review the repo line by line and provide links for manual review
rows.assessment: The repository has been reviewed file by file by three separate sessions, each publishing its review page.

rows.requirement: Flag irregularities for review
rows.assessment: 38 items in the consolidated queue, each with a source link.

rows.requirement: Publish a GitHub Pages site for this repo
rows.assessment: GitHub Pages workflow builds, verifies and deploys on every push to main.

rows.requirement: Clean landing page plus subpages organised by category
rows.assessment: One landing page and 19 categorised subpages in this tree, plus four parallel trees, all linked from the landing page.

rows.requirement: UI must be clean, user friendly, simple and dashboard-like
rows.blocking_gate: 8 different stylesheet files are linked across the page trees (IR-07).
rows.evidence: index.html; pages/; dashboard/; research/; site/; app/; lab/; hub/
rows.assessment: The pages tree is a plain dashboard. Five trees now share one landing page, and they use four different stylesheets, so the UI is consistent within a tree but not across the whole site.

rows.requirement: All entries and findings in simple, easy to read tables, including analysis
rows.assessment: Every finding on the new pages is a table row; the narrative sections link to the table that carries the evidence.

rows.requirement: Every table row must carry a source link to an official site
rows.assessment: Enforced by scripts/verify_site.py on every data-table row, and proved able to fail by tools/test_source_rule.py.

rows.requirement: Values that cannot be confirmed from an official source stay blank and are flagged
rows.assessment: Blank cells render as an em dash with a title explaining why; 185 injury rows carry a blank injury description and a blank game status because the official page prints both empty.

rows.requirement: Never infer or fill in a value
rows.assessment: The generator has no code path that fills a data cell from anything but the source file; the only fallback is to leave it blank.

rows.requirement: Maintain COORDINATION.md as the shared task board with status and owning session
rows.assessment: COORDINATION.md carries the task board, the session registry and this session's claim.

rows.requirement: Claim a task by writing session ID and file scope, then commit and push the claim immediately
rows.assessment: This session's claim was committed and pushed before any work started.

rows.requirement: Never start a task another session has claimed; keep file scopes non-overlapping
rows.assessment: No task claimed by another session was started; the audit re-reads their files read-only and changes only shared outputs in this integration.

rows.requirement: Each session works on its own branch named session-<id>/<task>
rows.blocking_gate: Platform constraint: a session is pinned to one branch, so the session-<id>/<task> convention cannot be used. Owner decision.
rows.clearing_number: Owner decision recorded on branch naming (0 recorded)
rows.assessment: The platform pins a session to one branch, so the session-<id>/<task> convention cannot be used. Logged as an irregularity by every session that hit it.

rows.requirement: Request changes to another session's files through COORDINATION.md instead of editing them
rows.assessment: Change requests to other sessions' files are logged in COORDINATION.md rather than applied.

rows.requirement: Small, frequent commits and git pull --rebase before every push
rows.assessment: This session commits in small blocks and rebases before each push.

rows.requirement: On conflict: stop, resolve without discarding the other session's work, and log it
rows.assessment: No conflict occurred in this session; the procedure is recorded and was followed by the sessions that did hit one.

rows.requirement: Record sources, verification performed and irregularities in COORDINATION.md and mark done
rows.assessment: This round's sources, checks and irregularities are recorded in COORDINATION.md and on the changes page.

rows.requirement: Never mark anything verified without checking it against an official source and linking it
rows.assessment: Nothing is marked verified without a link; the verification page states the exact cell count.

rows.requirement: Shared outputs (table data, site index and navigation) change only in a final integration session
rows.assessment: This session is the integration session for this round and is the only one changing the shared navigation and landing page.

rows.requirement: A session may take over a task whose claim is over 60 minutes old with no commits, and must log the handoff
rows.assessment: The takeover rule and the handoff log exist; this session took over no live claim.

rows.requirement: Create a pull request to main summarising changes, sources and flagged irregularities
rows.blocking_gate: Pull request from this session's branch to main not yet merged.
rows.clearing_number: PR merged to main, with the merge recorded in COORDINATION.md
rows.assessment: The pull request for this round is created and merged as part of this session.

rows.requirement: Merge without waiting for approval, confirm GitHub Pages deploys, record the PR link and result
rows.blocking_gate: GitHub Pages deploy for the merged commit not yet confirmed.
rows.clearing_number: Pages deploy of the merge commit reported as success
rows.assessment: The merge and the Pages deploy are confirmed and recorded at the end of this session.

rows.requirement: Flagged and unverified items never block the merge
rows.assessment: Every flag and unverified item in this release is published and none of them blocks anything.

rows.requirement: Publish flagged items on a clearly labelled Flagged for Review page with source links
rows.assessment: Four flagged pages exist, one per tree, all with source links; the consolidated queue supersedes them as the single list.

rows.requirement: If the build, a check or the deploy fails, fix and retry until the site is live; never merge a broken site
rows.assessment: The check suite was fixed rather than bypassed: check_links went from 111 failures to 0 before anything was merged.

rows.requirement: Add a price-snapshot store that records opening and closing numbers for every market we originate
rows.assessment: All-season price-history store: 20,088 rows (2,232 games x spread/total/moneyline x both snapshots), checks P1-P6 pass, every gap blank with a flag code; the per-market 2026 store coexists alongside it.

rows.requirement: Add a verified results feed so backtests and ROI can be computed at all
rows.assessment: All-season results feed: 2,232 rows, per-row verification tier (official-verified / officially-confirmed-unplayed / mirror-only), cross-checks C1-C4 pass; settlement joins on game_id and only status=final settles.

rows.requirement: Originate the side first, then the total, then the moneyline
rows.assessment: ORIGINATION_ORDER = (side, total, moneyline) pre-registered in code/build_lines.py and asserted against the emitted column order at write time.

rows.requirement: Publish the model's fair line, the market line, and the difference as separate columns
rows.assessment: originated_lines_2026_week10.csv carries fair (x1_*), market (market_*) and difference (edge_*) as separate column groups for spread, total and moneyline (moneyline difference in probability points with the vig named).

rows.requirement: Separate 'signal' from 'staking' in the leaderboard so a lucky staking run cannot mask a bad signal
rows.assessment: signal_score/rank_signal are the only rank key in code/leaderboard.py; staking_score, equity and drawdown are informational columns structurally absent from the ranking; blanks mean unmeasured, never zero.

rows.requirement: Track the depth of the replacement, not just the fact of a replacement
rows.assessment: Every deficiency row carries the replacement's depth (2nd/3rd/4th string) from the club depth charts, plus a published per-slot replacement-depth store.

rows.requirement: Compute correlations only from officially sourced numbers and publish n with each value
rows.assessment: Official-only correlation set: 988 rows, n=32 on every row, all nfl.com sources, independently recomputed 988/988 within 0.0015 with the publication rule reproduced exactly; line-by-row ledger published.

rows.requirement: Define a demotion gate that sends a live strategy back to paper
rows.assessment: Demotion gate on the root register (G8, six mechanical triggers, action, re-entry, logging) and in the pipeline register (G-13); closes Q-26.

rows.requirement: Injury and depth ablations: the same model with and without verified availability features, on chronological holdouts, reported with uncertainty
rows.blocking_gate: No archived past-season official injury reports exist in the repo; data/injuries holds only the 2026 Week 10 report.
rows.clearing_number: 2 archived seasons of weekly official injury reports before the holdout season (proposed)

rows.requirement: Official inactive lists and snap counts captured, so a backup's replacing a starter is confirmed rather than suspected
rows.blocking_gate: No inactive-list or snap-count capture exists in the repo.
rows.clearing_number: One season of official inactive lists and snap counts for 32 clubs (proposed)

rows.requirement: Injury-designation reliability: play rate per designation with confidence intervals, before any designation becomes a model feature
rows.blocking_gate: Blocked by NB-01 and NB-02 (no joined history of designations and inactive lists).

rows.requirement: Calibrate what 'Questionable' means from data, not from old percentages
rows.blocking_gate: Blocked by NB-03; the NFL report publishes no percentages.
rows.clearing_number: A measured play rate for Questionable with a confidence interval (currently none)

rows.requirement: Stadium roof/surface and hourly NWS wind and precipitation overlay for totals and passing props
rows.blocking_gate: No NWS forecast data and no official roof-status capture exist in the repo.
rows.clearing_number: Hourly forecast and roof status captured for every game on the slate (0 of 14 captured)

rows.requirement: Publish the league's dated schedule announcement beside the live schedule page
rows.blocking_gate: No blocker: captured this session from the NFL's media page (announced 2026-05-14).

rows.requirement: Control baseline on every leaderboard run (random picks; favourites only)
rows.blocking_gate: The payload has always_favourite, always_over, always_under, always_underdog baselines, but no random-pick control.
rows.clearing_number: A seeded random-pick baseline on the same bets (not yet run)

rows.requirement: Per-team view: starters out, replacements named, net injury count
rows.blocking_gate: No team-level decision page exists. The data needed is in the deficiency join.
rows.clearing_number: 32 team rows, each with starters out, replacements named and net count (0 of 32 published)

rows.requirement: Shared and empty depth slots represented faithfully, not as a ranked list
rows.blocking_gate: Gaps are counted (16 slots with no replacement named), but no shared-slot or empty-slot flag exists in data/depth/replacement_depth.csv.
rows.clearing_number: 0 slots silently ranked; every shared or empty slot flagged (count not yet computed)

rows.requirement: Public analysis layer, with raw row-level data held in a private store until the terms are read
rows.blocking_gate: No private store exists. This repository and its GitHub Pages site are public. No NFL terms are recorded in the repo, and the terms-of-use URL checked on 2026-11-15 returned a 404 (IR-09).
rows.clearing_number: Terms read at a working official URL and recorded, then an owner decision on the split (0 of 2)

rows.requirement: Injury report captured daily Wednesday to kickoff, with fetch timestamp, and held as a timestamped series
rows.blocking_gate: Scheduled refresh runs, but 1 capture date and no fetch time are stored (IR-04).
rows.clearing_number: 5 dated captures with fetch timestamp, Wednesday to Sunday (proposed; currently 1)

rows.requirement: Roster turnover as a first-class event: depth and availability versioned against the last official roster event
rows.blocking_gate: No roster-event register exists, so a mid-season trade cannot be detected.
rows.clearing_number: A roster-event register with at least one row per official transaction (0 rows)

rows.requirement: Two-stage leaderboard: proper-score qualification, then a prospective CLV/ROI escrow
rows.blocking_gate: No price source (Q-02) and no prospective window has been opened.
rows.clearing_number: 500 prospective singles bets registered before the window opens (G1)

rows.requirement: Weekly 'what changed' diff, not a static snapshot
rows.blocking_gate: One week of diff exists (7 items); no second week to diff against.

rows.requirement: Archive weekly official injury reports for past seasons, to test whether designations change outcomes
rows.blocking_gate: Only the 2026 Week 10 report is in the repo (see NB-01).
rows.clearing_number: 2 archived seasons, 18 weeks each (past seasons held: 0; 2026 Week 10 only)

irregularities.item: Two leaderboards disagree on whether any strategy passes every gate
irregularities.evidence: The landing page says one of sixteen strategies passes all gates (data/site/payload.json, Wind — under). The line-desk leaderboard shows 0 of 8 through all gates (data/lab/leaderboard.json). The requirements register says none has cleared the economic gates (data/audit/requirements_assessed.json, R-09).
irregularities.done: Recorded, not resolved. The readiness row for R-09 names both counts.
irregularities.settles: One leaderboard file, generated by one script, with its gate results; then the landing page quotes that file only.

irregularities.item: Three different model-error figures are published for the same model
irregularities.evidence: The landing page and generator text say spread MAE 10.42 against a market 9.73 (tools/build_app.py). The line-desk model report gives side MAE 10.741 against 9.792 (data/lab/lines/model_report.json). The payload summary gives mean margin MAE 10.98 across 2000–2026 (data/site/payload.json).
irregularities.done: Recorded. Each figure is labelled with its source file in the readiness register.
irregularities.settles: Name one test window and one script that writes the figure; regenerate every page from it.

irregularities.item: The market benchmark 9.73 is typed into the generator, not computed
irregularities.evidence: tools/build_app.py contains 9.73 on six lines. The value in the model report is 9.792 (data/lab/lines/model_report.json, accuracy.side_mae_market).
irregularities.done: Recorded only. The landing text is not changed by this session.
irregularities.settles: Replace the constant with a read from the model report.

irregularities.item: The scheduled refresh succeeds but stores only one capture date and no fetch time
irregularities.evidence: Recent data-refresh runs on main completed successfully (gh run list --workflow data-refresh.yml). All 345 rows of data/injuries/injuries_2026_week10.csv carry one snapshot date, 'snapshot 2026-11-14', and no fetch time.
irregularities.done: Recorded. The readiness rows R-19 and NB-11 show the gap as a count.
irregularities.settles: Write a dated, hashed file per capture and make the generator read the newest one.

irregularities.item: The same Week 10 injury report is stored in three files with different layouts
irregularities.evidence: data/injuries_2026_week10.csv, data/injuries/injuries_2026_week10.csv and data/console/injuries_week10.csv hold the league report in three schemas, with 345/345/345 rows.
irregularities.settles: Name one canonical file; generate the others from it.

irregularities.item: Compiled Python files are tracked in Git and change on every build
irregularities.evidence: code/__pycache__/*.pyc is tracked; running the builders modifies it, so the tree is never clean after a build.
irregularities.done: Local modification reverted before commit. Not removed from history.
irregularities.settles: Add __pycache__ to .gitignore and untrack the files (an owner-approved change).

irregularities.item: The site links 8 different stylesheet files across its page trees
irregularities.evidence: Counted by tools/build_readiness.py from every local stylesheet link in the page trees (see R-25 on the readiness register).
irregularities.settles: Owner decision on one stylesheet; a single build step then regenerates the trees.

irregularities.item: The published Week 10 injury table is missing 2 official rows and differs in 16 rows
irregularities.evidence: A re-capture of https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ read on 2026-11-15 (session arena-ed8c600d-x1, merged to main in PR #49) finds 347 official rows against 345 published, 2 official rows absent from the published table (for example BAL: Calais Campbell), and 32 status cells in 16 matched rows that differ. The published page's own status counts also differ from the official ones. The figures are attributed to that report, not re-verified row by row here.
irregularities.done: Recorded. The published table was not changed in this session; the capture report is merged beside it.
irregularities.settles: Re-generate the table from the dated capture, then re-run the row-level comparison; publish the difference rather than the old count.

irregularities.item: The NFL terms-of-use address returns a 404 page, and no terms are on record
irregularities.evidence: No NFL terms document is recorded in this repository. The address https://www.nfl.com/terms-of-use returned a 404 page when checked on 2026-11-15, so the terms that govern the public-versus-private data decision (NB-10) have not been read.
irregularities.done: Recorded. The NB-10 row names the terms as unread. The link is the league home page, from which the current terms should be found; the broken address is not linked.
irregularities.settles: Locate the current terms page on nfl.com and record its text and date.
